result.title: An all-transistor physical-learning transformer can be trained to perform in-context learning
result.summary: Most systems trained by equilibrium propagation or coupled learning are in the same class as multi-layer perceptrons: while they may be universal function approximators, they struggle to learn associative tasks which are easy for transformers. Equilibrium propagation relies on a bidirectional flow of information through the physical system between input and output. The reverse flow is broken by more complex nonlinear systems, such as those performing multiplication which is needed to express dot-product attention. Here we explicitly restore this bidirectional flow by introducing extra circuit elements for this purpose into a double or dyadic circuit. We then use these ideas to construct an attention mechanism exploiting the exponential current law of sub-threshold MOSFET devices. We show that in simulations this circuit can be trained to perform a simple in-context learning task, despite using realistic reverse components which transmit only an approximate gradient. For this training to succeed we need cross-entropy loss (not mean squared error). We generate nudges appropriate for this loss using a novel floating circuit element, based on the same MOSFET sub-circuit used for softmax. We train the resistors in this circuit using the Lion optimiser, which can be implemented using one capacitor per parameter to store local memory of past gradient estimates.

AI.brief_summary: 论文设计一种全晶体管「物理学习」transformer 电路：借助 dyadic 电路中的额外元件恢复 equilibrium propagation 所需的双向信息流，利用亚阈值 MOSFET 的指数电流律实现注意力与 softmax，并通过仿真训练其电阻完成简单 in-context learning。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 equilibrium propagation 局部信用分配、仅传近似梯度的反向元件、以及按交叉熵损失构造 nudge 信号的训练机制，或可对应 LVR 中 latent 状态的训练监督与贡献分配问题，属可供核查的方法线索；但论文本身面向模拟硬件与 in-context learning，未涉及视觉或多模态推理。
